sentences.text: HONOURABLE
MS. JUSTICE S.V. PINTO
Date : 16/06/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT
This appeal has been preferred by the appellant - Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., - org. opponent No.3 against the respondent Nos.1 to 4-original claimants, respondent Nos.5 and NEUTRAL CITATION C
/FA/3520/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined 6-original opponent Nos.1 and 2 and respondent nos.7 to 9 - org.

opponent nos.4 to 6 under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short the Act) being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award passed by the learned MACT (AUX), Vadodara in MACP No.1427 of 1993 on 04/10/2006..

The parties herein are referred to as they stood in the original claim petition for the sake of brevity,
clarity and convenience.

2. At the outset, it is required to be noted that initially two claim petitions were filed out of the accident being MACP No.1427 of 1993 and 1428 of 1993 and the appellant - insurance company had challenged both the claim petitions by filing First Appeal No.3520 of 2007 and 3521 of 2007 wherein First Appeal No.3521 of 2007 came to be disposed of vide order dated 31/07/2007 as not pressed without prejudicing the rights and contentions of the appellant-insurance company of the present appeal.
3.

entities.text: First Appeal No.3520 of 2007 and 3521 of 2007
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
The brief facts that emerge from the record are as under:
3.1 That on 23/12/1992 at about 9:15 pm deceased - Mehmood Hussen and injured-Hamidabanu were the pillion riders on the scooter No.GJ6H 1632 driven by the opponent no.4 and were going from Dabhoi to Vadodara and they reached near Kelanpur by maintaining moderate speed of the scooter on the correct side of the road where there is a bridge at the place of the accident and it was dark; wherein in the middle of the road truck bearing Registration No.GJ-17T-4655 was parked by the opponent no.1 without any parking lights,
back lights or side-

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3520/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined signals on and since the opponent no.4 realized that he will dash with the parking truck, he jumped out at the last moment from the scooter and the deceased alongwith the scooter dashed with the parked truck and sustained serious injuries and he was taken for treatment to Kelanpur Chokdi where he succumbed to his injuries.

4. The claimant Nos.1 and 2 - the parents of the deceased and claimant nos.3 and 4 - the sisters of the deceased filed the claim petition being MACP No.1427 of 1993 mainly stating that they had lost the sole earning member of the family and claimed an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- under all available heads jointly and severally from all the opponents.

sentences.text: Notices were duly served to all the opponents and the opponent no.3-insurance company appeared and filed its written statements at Exh.27.
6. The opponent no.3 - insurance company mainly denied all the contents of the claim petition.

7. The learned tribunal after having considered the evidence on record held the opponent Nos.1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and held that the accident occurred due to 100%
negligence on the part of the driver of the truck and granted an amount of Rs.3,36,000/- to the claimants with 7.5% interest from the date of the application till the realization.

The learned tribunal has considered the income of Rs.1,500/- per month and added 100% prospective income and deducted 1/3rd for personal expenses and granted future loss of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3520/2007 JUDGMENT

DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined dependency of Rs.3,06,000/- after applying multiplier of 17 and also granted an amount of Rs.25,000/- as loss of expectancy of life and love and affection and amount of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses.
8. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said award, the appellant - org. opponent no.3 - insurance company of truck has filed the present appeal before this Court.
9. I have heard learned Advocate Mr.Nanavati appearing for the appellant and Mr.Hakim for the contesting respondents.

10. It is mainly contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that admittedly the deceased was driving the scooter bearing Registration No.GJ-6H-1632 which had two pillion riders and the accident took place on 23/12/1992 at about 9:15 pm with the stationary truck bearing Registration No.GJ-17T-4655 lying on the road and the learned tribunal has not considered that the driver of the scooter jumped out of the scooter without applying the brakes to the scooter and as a result of which the entire incident took place; the learned tribunal has also not appreciated the fact that the scooter did have a front light and if the driver of the scooter was riding the scooter with moderate speed, the collusion could have been avoided.

Moreover there was sufficient space on the left hand side of the truck but the scooter rammed into the truck which candidly proves that the driver of the scooter was driving the scooter in excessive speed and he had to leave the pillion riders to their fate while he himself jumped from the scooter; that the driver of the scooter NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3520/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined has not deposed before the learned tribunal and the learned tribunal has failed to appreciate that more caution was expected from the driver of the scooter and 70% negligence to the driver of the scooter ought to have been awarded by the learned tribunal and the learned tribunal has grossly erred in coming to the conclusion and therefore the appeal must be allowed.

11. I have gone through the judgment of the present appeal where-from it appears that the claimant of MACP No.1428 of 1993 who is the eye-witness to the accident has deposed before the learned tribunal at Exh.34 and the witness has clearly stated that when they reached on the bridge near Kelanpur, it was dark and at around 9:15 pm the scooter was being driven on its correct side in normal speed and the truck bearing GJ-17T-4655 was kept stationary on the road without the lights on and there were no obstacles in front of or behind the truck;

that it as it was dark nothing could be Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sharifbhai Mahmadbhai Rakhiwala on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53805843/
3 seen and the scooter dashed behind the truck; that they were injured and taken to SSG Hospital wherein the deceased died on the spot.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the cross-examination of the witness, nothing to controvert this version has come on record and if the Panchnama which is produced at Exh.52 is perused, it can be seen that the truck was full of sand and the jack was placed below the wheels of the truck and the scooter was lying below the truck.

It is pertinent to note that the driver of the truck has not been examined by the insurance company before the learned tribunal and the driver of the truck had kept the truck stationary on the road and there were no lights or side- signals on or there were no obstacles placed on the road.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3520/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 undefined 12.

The main challenge in the appeal is with regard to the negligence of 100% attributed to the driver of the truck but if the evidence on record is considered, the learned tribunal has appreciated the evidence of the eye-witness i.e. claimant of MACP No.1428 of 1993 and the Panchnama and has found that the driver of the truck had kept the truck stationary without any signals or side-signals on in the dark at around 9:15 pm and no obstacles were placed behind the truck and thus the learned tribunal has not committed any error in awarding the compensation and the learned tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence and no error is said to have been committed.
13. For the forgoing reasons, no substance is found in the present appeal which would call for any interference.
Accordingly, while confirming the impugned judgment and award, the present appeal stands dismissed.
